# Technical notes

For installation and screenshots, see the [project README](../README.md).

## Interface and toolbar lifecycle

The popup and reading panel share design tokens from `src/ui-theme.ts`. The popup uses a 380 px layout capped at 580 px with vertical scrolling; the reading panel retains its closed shadow root, selectable Japanese text, native ruby, width controls, and saved appearance settings. Playgrounds temporarily uses the full panel height, with one scroll container and separate input/browser and tool views. Returning restores the reading scroll position; catalogue back navigation restores its own scroll and focus. Text-field CSS is scoped away from checkbox controls. The brutalist theme changes extension controls and surfaces, not webpage overlay geometry or page-native colors. The outlined 考 logo is rasterized into active, paused, and unavailable PNGs without a runtime font or graphics dependency.

About Kō includes a native expandable What’s new · Changelog section, open by default, and an offline release-history page. `docs/release-notes.md` is the shared source: the build selects the manifest version's entry, renders it into the About template, generates `dist/release-notes.html`, and writes `dist/docs/github-release-<version>.md` with absolute GitHub links for the release body. A missing or duplicate current-version entry fails the build. The opening paragraph of the current entry also supplies the popup’s compact update summary; keep it brief. The banner links to About and saves `dismissedUpdate:<manifest version>` as a boolean in local storage only when Close succeeds. Opening notes does not dismiss it. Storage changes synchronize open menus; a failed save leaves a retryable announcement. A new version uses a new key. About’s feature-suggestion link opens a prefilled GitHub issue without submitting it. Notes are bundled HTML with no runtime fetch or extra dependency. Both release ZIPs include the offline history; the generated release-body Markdown is a publishing artifact and is excluded from those ZIPs.

The background's toolbar controller uses per-tab `chrome.action.setIcon` and `setTitle`. Global pause takes precedence, followed by hostname pause, then supported HTTP/HTTPS URL and top-frame availability. A missing receiver requests a reload; unavailable Docs geometry or a tokenizer failure supplies its diagnostic reason. The action stays clickable in all states. No additional permissions or persisted settings are required.

The typed `status` response includes `toolbarAvailability` (`ready` or `unavailable`) independently of transient processing state. Initialization and changes in availability send `toolbar-status-changed`; only top-frame notifications trigger a fresh status probe. Routine scans, scrolling, IME composition, and hidden tabs do not toggle readiness. Navigation resets the icon while a new document loads; same-document URL updates recheck the existing document. Preference changes, activation, navigation completion, installation, browser startup, and each fresh service worker also refresh state. Per-tab revision tokens discard stale probes and late results for removed tabs. There is no continuous toolbar polling or source-text persistence.

## Kōくん companion · 1.3.0

Version `1.3.0` is the stable GitHub release dated 22 October 2026. Chrome Web Store submission and publication are managed separately. The build bundles the companion, its 56 PS1 sprite strips, static fallback, Japanese pixel font and license, plus the offline animation gallery. Both release ZIP layouts include the same runtime, including `animations.html` and `animations.js`; QA source sheets, previews, development notes and source maps remain outside the ZIPs.

`src/mascot.ts` owns one closed-shadow-root companion in the top-level webpage viewport. `mascot-motion.ts` handles pose paths, scheduling, clip timing and local movement; `mascot-target.ts`, `mascot-lookup.ts` and `mascot-bubble.ts` provide source-word targeting, offline analysis and the word bubble. The companion starts off, independently of automatic page furigana. Site pause hides it; hidden tabs suspend playback, printing/fullscreen hide it, and system reduced motion or the still option overrides movement. Dragging and keyboard placement save a normalized position per hostname, with bounded storage and validated mutations through the shared preference writer. Existing corrections and reading preferences retain their formats.

Standing and seated rests retain authored breathing/blinks; sleep holds a still frame and uses a low-frequency timer. Ordinary rests last 12–24 seconds, with sleep eligible only after three active minutes and three walks. A click or Enter/Space enables a 60-second wall-clock wake interval, refreshed rather than stacked, with 8–16 second rests. Eight special routines rotate after a 5–10 minute active-time cooldown. A word reading immediately selects the open-scroll loop, settling airborne movement while preserving the saved ground position. Clip decoding uses a six-strip cache with the reading loop retained. See the [1.3 verification notes](release-1.3-audit.md) for timing and movement details.

Hover lookup waits 600 ms and follows the resolved word's bounds; leaving it dismisses the bubble. Highlight mode accepts one Japanese word. Webpage text, accessible open shadows, exposed Docs geometry and reading-panel word hooks supply targets. Browser-protected pages, PDFs, embedded frames and arbitrary image/canvas text are unsupported. Mascot analysis uses its own `mascot` request purpose and cancellation channel. Definitions start off. English uses the complete bundled JMdict dictionary first, with English Wiktionary fallback on a local miss or asset failure; Japanese uses a bundled Japanese Wiktionary snapshot, with the same online fallback rule. Reading-panel languages load independently, so local English is not delayed by Japanese. The `define-word` message still accepts an omitted language for a bilingual reply. Readings and saved corrections stay local, and lookup failures leave them available.

The About version is a visually subdued native button. Its fifth activation navigates to `animations.html` in the same tab, so browser Back returns to About. `src/animations.ts` reads the bundled mascot manifest and groups all clips into 24 routines and six transitions. Thirty labeled canvas tiles play entry/loop/exit sequences automatically, without controls or stored preferences. Tiles load on entering the viewport and stop advancing offscreen; hidden tabs suspend playback and reduced motion shows each tile's first frame. The gallery makes no network requests.

## Reading customization

Open **Reading appearance** in the popup to choose Small, Default, Large, or Extra large readings and page colors or high contrast. These choices are saved per hostname. Readings still shrink or disappear where necessary to preserve the original layout.

Open **Local reading corrections** to save, edit, or remove a word and its reading. Hiragana and katakana input are accepted; readings display in hiragana. Corrections apply automatically across sites and persist on this device. Longest matches take priority, including names spanning several dictionary tokens. Up to 200 corrections are supported; words and readings are limited to 80 characters each. Corrected phrases are separated before dictionary analysis so neighboring words retain their own readings.

In a word detail card, **Correct reading** opens a form prefilled with the exact surface and effective pronunciation, including saved multi-token corrections. This form is independent of online definition availability. **Restore automatic reading** removes a saved exact-word correction. Panel input and composition events never trigger page rescans.

The popup filters corrections by word or reading (katakana queries normalize to hiragana). Backups use `{version:1, corrections:{...}}` JSON and contain no settings or extracted text. Imports are capped at 256 KiB, validate every entry before writing, normalize readings, preserve existing values on conflicts, and reject imports exceeding 200 corrections without partial writes. No downloads permission is needed for export.

Correction saves, renames, deletions, and imports share a single service-worker read/modify/write queue with reading-panel preferences, site pauses, and site appearance patches. Independent popup windows and top-frame HTTP/HTTPS content scripts send validated mutation messages; each operation reads the latest stored state when its turn begins. Failed operations do not block later ones. The storage schema and backup format are unchanged.

The status distinguishes tight spacing, unknown dictionary words, unavailable Docs geometry, no visible kanji, waiting during editing/scrolling, and the view limit. It describes the bounded text discovered in the current view, not every word in the full document.

## Extra-space reading view

On a webpage or Google Doc, open **Reading view** in the popup and enable **Extra-space reading view**. Activation is remembered per hostname. Choose Comfortable, Roomy, or Spacious spacing and 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, or 32 px text (default 20 px). Drag the left edge to resize, or focus the edge and use Left/Right (10 px steps), Home, or End. Width defaults to 420 px and is bounded to 280–720 px and the available viewport. Spacing, text size, and width are shared across sites. Width saves when a drag finishes; appearance updates do not retokenize or replace panel content.

Use **Close** or turn off the option to return to overlays for that hostname. Global pause and the site exclusion also hide the panel. One panel runs in the top frame; embedded-frame text is not aggregated.

This is a separate, selectable text-only reading panel with native ruby. It replaces the extension's in-document overlays while active, and does not resize, restyle, or edit the original editor. Continue editing in Docs; the panel updates after scrolling and editing settle. Only visible webpage text, or the active Docs page's visible text (the editor viewport in pageless documents), is extracted, up to 16,000 characters / 2,000 runs and 500 reading candidates. Panel scrolling is independent. Inactive pages are never tokenized. Text without kanji remains visible. Existing appearance preferences and local corrections also apply.

Webpage extraction reuses bounded discovery, restores DOM/composed-tree order, and groups inline text by block. Wrapped text is split only at visibility boundaries and reflows in the panel. Extension content is excluded and hit-testing can discover text beneath the panel. Editable controls and existing ruby retain the overlay exclusions.

The panel simplifies formatting and tables, omits images, and depends on the same annotated Docs text geometry as overlays. It cannot recover unavailable geometry. Routine refreshes wait for at least 400 ms of quiet, keeping the previous text and open definition visible until the replacement is ready. Identical text and readings do not rebuild the panel, preserving selection, keyboard focus, scroll position, and definitions across Docs tile redraws. Composition and unavailable text still clear the panel; disabling it or hiding the tab removes it immediately. It is hidden during printing. The `readingView` setting contains `sites`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, and `width`. If absent, legacy `docsReadingView` enables only docs.google.com and supplies its spacing; the new format is persisted on the next preference change. Preferences are stored locally; extracted document text stays in memory.

Panel words are click targets using Kuromoji token boundaries and base forms, including kana-only words. Corrections spanning multiple tokens keep their ruby and click target together. Click or use Tab and Enter/Space to open word details and automatically load definitions; Escape or its close button dismisses them and returns focus. Available playground controls are computed from the same snapshot. The word action reads Try word forms for a supported verb or adjective, and Open playgrounds for other tools. Word activation automatically loads English and Japanese definitions separately, with source links and JMdict or Wiktionary attribution. No separate lookup button appears during loading or after a successful or missing result. Missing entries, unsupported source layouts, and network errors are reported per language; a Retry definitions online button retries only the failed language. Updates and closing invalidate pending UI results.

Activating a reading-panel word or retrying a failed language sends a `define-word` message. The service worker accepts only top-frame HTTP/HTTPS content-script requests, validates the term and language, and returns structured plain-text senses and source metadata. Local English hits make no external request. The complete pinned English JMdict snapshot is imported with Python 3's standard library into 256 deterministic gzip-compressed JSON shards. Each shard indexes NFC-normalized spellings/readings and retains entry IDs, priority tags, reading/spelling restrictions, usage labels, and sense restrictions. Shards load lazily in the service worker, with at most 16 retained and an 8 MiB source-text cache weight limit; parsed objects add overhead. The original tokenizer and lemma recovery are unchanged.

Japanese definitions use 256 additional compressed shards, imported from pinned Japanese-language JSONL rows of the Kaikki/Wiktextract raw Japanese Wiktionary export. The importer retains source titles, parts of speech, readings and sense labels, and joins hierarchical gloss context. Unique explicit spelling references are resolved at build time with cycle detection and an eight-hop limit; ambiguous/unresolved references remain online misses. General kana aliases are not inferred from readings, avoiding homophone conflation. Entries without glosses and unexpanded template markup are excluded. Both dictionaries share the same bounded shard cache and result cache. Source preparation and ordinary builds use Python's standard library and verify pinned checksums; runtime packages exclude source JSONL. See the [Japanese source notes](../data/jawiktionary/README.md).

Online fallback uses the selected Wiktionary Action API with omitted credentials/referrer and no HTTP redirects. Parsing occurs only in the shared offscreen document using an inert template; remote HTML never enters a live content-script panel. Recognized spelling references, including English nested `ja-see` tables and Japanese `和語の漢字表記` lists, may resolve one unique canonical term within the same edition. Resolution permits two reference hops, detects cycles, caps each response at 1 MB, and shares one eight-second deadline across fetches, offscreen creation, and parsing. Unknown page structures are retryable failures rather than cached missing words.

Concurrent language-specific lookups are deduplicated and capped at eight active jobs. The shared service-worker result cache holds at most 256 entries: successful definitions last until eviction or worker shutdown, genuine misses expire after five minutes, and failures are never cached. The panel displays up to four senses of 600 characters per language; the companion displays up to two. Stale results cannot replace a newer selection. Neither definition queries nor results are persisted as history. The surrounding sentence and document are never sent; online editorial references can send up to two additional canonical lookup terms. See the [local-dictionary verification report](../qa/release-1.3/local-dictionary.md) for source details, tests, package sizes, and measured harness timings.

## Local exploration

Word metadata optionally includes part of speech, independent/helper classification, conjugation class/form for known inflecting tokens, and a verb's dictionary-form reading. Auxiliary endings retain their class/form so phrase recognition can distinguish supported endings from unsupported continuations. Dictionary-form readings are cached for at most 256 verbs and are derived only in reading-panel and explicit playground-analysis jobs; automatic overlay jobs do not do this extra work.

Verb Playground uses reviewed finite form families, bounded to 12 starts, 12 adjacent tokens, 80 source characters, and 128 variants per candidate. Exact spelling, reading, and family-specific terminal morphology must reproduce the source. Ambiguous interpretations and possible potential bases require explicit choices; unresolved derived lemmas have restricted controls. Meaning Forks retains its small finite token grammar. Mimetic Playground matches 90 canonical expressions with explicit aliases and width/script normalization, including contiguous token-aligned expressions. Each expression has a bundled twelve-frame WebP strip in a ukiyo-e-inspired low-poly pixel style. The manifest exposes only `art/mimetics/*.webp` to HTTP/HTTPS pages so content-script reading panels can display local artwork; no script, dictionary, setting, or user data is exposed by that resource rule. The exhaustive original SVG registry remains available through the About page’s **Show legacy animations** switch. All tools use safe DOM/text rendering and the existing closed shadow root. Source changes dismiss exploration and pending analysis; identical redraws retain its controls. Saved corrections suppress overlapping grammar explorations.

The popup header opens `playgrounds.html` in a standalone extension tab; the reading-panel header still opens the same shared dictionary-form verb/adjective input and browser of 90 mimetic expressions in 45 comparisons. The standalone tab works without webpage access, automatic readings, or Reading view. It lazily creates its own bundled tokenizer worker on the first word-form query, cancels pending work on input changes and page exit, and terminates the worker when closed. Mimetics browsing needs no dictionary worker. The page observes the same legacy-animation preference as the reading panel. There is no preset verb list; words come from explicit typed input or clicked words in the reading panel. Mimetic search uses bundled Japanese, readings, and English keywords. Typed dictionary words are checked on explicit submission and confirmed before generation. Existing tokenize/cancel messages accept an optional purpose of readings (the default) or playground. Playground batches are limited to four nonempty strings of at most 40 characters each, request word metadata, and ignore pronunciation overrides. Replacement and cancellation match both document owner and purpose; the worker uses separate tab/purpose cache keys. Word-form input introduces no new network origin, permission, external service, storage format, or persistent setting.

See [exploration notes](exploration-notes.md) for the supported language families and references. The bundled kamiya-codec 4.16.1 generator is pinned and ships with its Unlicense text. Original mimetic examples and legacy vector artwork are included directly in the content bundle. New generated raster animations are loaded on demand from packaged `art/mimetics/*.webp` resources, exposed to HTTP/HTTPS pages through the manifest’s narrowly scoped web-accessible resource declaration. They require no remote requests. Animations start automatically and loop continuously (2.4 seconds per cycle for the generated artwork), with no replay button. Motion is disabled by prefers-reduced-motion. Static views show the middle pose. The global local-storage boolean `showLegacyAnimations` defaults to false; storage changes replace only the scene in open cards, preserving selected words and focus. Generated-art prompts and assembly metadata live in `qa/mimetics-generation/`.

## Google Docs compatibility

The Docs adapter supports paged and pageless editors, including padded text rectangles and overlapping tiles.

Docs renders text on canvas, so ordinary webpage text extraction does not work there. The adapter sets `_docs_annotate_canvas_by_ext` to its own extension ID at document start and reads annotated SVG rectangles, their `aria-label` text, and `data-font-css` font metadata. These are undocumented Google internals and can change or be unavailable. If text geometry is unavailable, the toolbar status says so; the extension never substitutes guessed text or remotely processes a document. It does not impersonate another extension.

Only **one active page** is annotated: the page with the largest visible area in the browser viewport, retaining the current page on ties. IntersectionObserver tracks page visibility; inactive page text never goes to the tokenizer. In pageless documents, only visible text in the editor region is processed. Glyph ink measurements, rather than padded line boxes, determine free space for readings. Duplicate tile runs are suppressed and readings are clipped to the editor region. Scrolling clears old annotations immediately and rebuilds them once scrolling stops. The adapter watches the hidden same-origin Docs input iframe for IME composition and input events.

To verify live compatibility, load the extension, reload a Japanese Google Doc, and check the popup status. Exercise editing/viewing, IME input, undo/redo, tables, browser zoom, Docs zoom, and paged/pageless layouts. Confirm readings stay on the visible active page, selection/copying work normally, and no text or formatting edits appear in document history. A compatible annotated SVG surface and font metadata are required.

## Performance and behavior

- Webpage discovery uses viewport hit-testing, with at most 512 seed elements, 128 traversal steps per seed, and 4,096 total traversal steps per pass. It does not walk every offscreen sibling in a huge flat document.
- Docs discovers page containers once and incrementally observes new containers. It measures only visible page candidates and extracts only the active page's visible text.
- Maximum 2,000 characters per reading-tokenizer batch and one in-flight tokenizer batch per tab (with at most 32 queued requests); playground batches have the smaller four-by-40-character limit. Maximum 500 annotation candidates per frame. Cross-origin frames have independent controllers. Dictionary caches are separated by tab/purpose and capped at 2,000 entries / 200,000 retained characters (including readings) per cache.
- Docs geometry is measured once per scan; repeated prefix widths and glyph measurements are cached within that scan. A screen-cell collision index checks nearby glyphs instead of comparing every annotation against all visible text.
- Geometry/discovery cooperatively yields at a 4 ms target, reduced to 2 ms during activity bursts; individual browser layout operations may exceed that budget. Initial layout of an enormous page is still the browser's responsibility.
- Overlay content changes wait for at least 150 ms of quiet and scrolling for at least 100 ms. The reading panel uses a minimum 400 ms trailing debounce for routine updates. Rapid activity extends these waits up to 500 ms for edits / 450 ms for scrolling, then returns to normal. Explicit settings and visibility changes remain immediate. New activity cancels pending work for the originating document; canceled queued jobs never reach the worker. In-progress batches stop between dictionary calls; a single synchronous call (at most 2,000 characters) and initial dictionary loading cannot be interrupted. Stale results are discarded; background tabs stop scheduling work. No polling loop runs while idle.
- Original text nodes, line spacing, editor values, and document formatting are never changed. Added overlay elements live outside the editor. They ignore mouse input, are excluded from selection and the accessibility tree, and are hidden in print output.
- Readings are hiragana. Kana endings are aligned where unambiguous; ambiguous alignment uses a whole-word reading. For an isolated Japanese headword or a translation line such as `出口 = salida` (also `＝`, `:`, or `：`, with a Latin-script gloss), a proper-name analysis is replaced with the lowest-cost exact common-noun entry when available. Sentences and names with surrounding text keep normal dictionary analysis; a standalone name can still be ambiguous. Saved corrections take priority, and original context is retained across correction fragments. Unknown readings are omitted. Names and ambiguous words may be read incorrectly.
- Furigana shrinks to fit available width and spacing, down to 6 px in Docs and 7 px on webpages, then is omitted if too small or colliding. Tight line spacing can prevent annotations from appearing. No reflow is introduced.
- Bounded discovery can omit text in exceptionally dense/complex viewports. Overlay word fragments spanning multiple lines are skipped; the panel can reflow wrapped webpage text. Vertical writing, rotated text, images, PDFs, arbitrary canvas apps, browser-protected pages, and closed shadow roots are unsupported. Webpage editable controls and existing ruby are skipped.

Enabled/excluded-site preferences, per-hostname appearance, reading-view settings, the legacy-animation choice, per-version update-announcement dismissals, and user-entered reading corrections are persisted in `chrome.storage.local`. Automatically extracted source text, reading caches, and clicked-word definition caches stay in memory. The extension-page CSP allows packaged resources and the two Wiktionary origins used for definition lookups when a word is activated. Google Docs itself still uses its normal network connection.

## Develop and test

Use Node.js 26.12.1 from `.nvmrc`, or a patched version in the 22.x (22.23.4+), 24.x (24.22.1+), or 26.x (26.12.1+) lines. The engine requirement is enforced during npm installation, builds (including packaging), typechecks, and tests. See the [October 2026 security review](security-review-2026-10.md).

```sh
nvm install
nvm use
npm ci
npm run build
npm run typecheck
npm test
```

Build output is `dist/`, including the bundled dictionaries, companion assets, and bundles and third-party notices. No CDN assets are needed at runtime. Dependency downloads occur only during development installation.

Integration tests run the actual extension in a temporary Chromium profile and use a localhost fixture server. By default they use Brave at its standard macOS path; set `CHROMIUM_PATH` to an extension-capable Chromium executable on other machines. Chrome distributions that disable command-line extension loading cannot run these tests. Tests do not use or modify your normal browser profile or Google account.

Coverage includes automatic readings, mixed inline markup, unchanged source/layout, dynamic updates, toggles/exclusions, print hiding, IME suspension, a 100,000-node webpage, a 100-page synthetic Docs document, dense pageless Docs lines, duplicate tile suppression, editor clipping, reading alignment, cache eviction, cancellation isolation, adaptive pacing, correction validation, automatic corrections, per-site appearance, diagnostic states, and the optional webpage/Docs reading panel (spacing, editing updates, active-page switching, source preservation, and closing). Bilingual definition fixtures cover automatic requests on word activation, base forms, kana-only words, language filtering, unsafe markup, keyboard access, cache reuse, per-language errors, missing entries, retries, and stale lookups. Additional fixtures cover wrapped webpage text, panel occlusion, per-site activation, font/width persistence, pointer and keyboard resizing, offline corrections/restoration, multi-token readings, correction search, backup export/import failures, and legacy settings migration.

Playground checks cover golden verb/adjective forms and changing readings, real-dictionary class alternatives and phrase recognition, ambiguity choices, contextual imperative recovery, contractions, exact Reset, all 90 mimetic assets and aliases, token-boundary joins, confirmed typed input, purpose-isolated cancellation, stale results, keyboard operation, 280–720 px layouts, and reduced motion. Tests exercise both the default pixel animations and legacy line style, automatic looping, live style changes, and offline decoding. Update-announcement checks verify local per-version dismissal across browser restart, synchronized open menus, save-failure recovery, offline changelog access, and the GitHub suggestion destination. The native popup check verifies its 580 px height, announcement, dismissal, and wheel access to footer links. Existing concurrency, source-preservation, hidden/disclosure, and lexical-kana regressions remain covered. See the [1.2 release audit](release-1.2-audit.md) for historical results; see the [1.3 audit](release-1.3-audit.md) for current packaging evidence. Historical live read-only Docs evidence is retained in the [1.1 audit](chrome-web-store-audit.md); live editing was not exercised for RC1.

Original project code, documentation, and assets in the 1.3.0 distribution use the [Kō No-Resale License 1.0](../LICENSE). Free use (including at work), modification, and free sharing are permitted; paid distribution, paid access, and inclusion in paid products require the owner's written permission, including for modified or rebranded copies. Earlier MIT-distributed copies retain their original permissions. Third-party licenses are included in `dist/licenses/`: Kuromoji (Apache 2.0), IPADIC (its own notice), async, doublearray, zlibjs, lodash, and kamiya-codec (Unlicense). JMdict data and derived shards retain CC BY-SA 4.0 separately from Kō; EDRDG attribution, licence text, source metadata, and dictionary documentation ship under `dist/licenses/jmdict/`. The pinned source gzip is kept under `data/jmdict/` and is excluded from runtime ZIPs. Ordinary builds make no dictionary downloads; refresh the snapshot before releases using the [documented procedure](../data/jmdict/README.md). The URL-safe dictionary path adapter and reviewed conjugation adapter are local project code; upstream dependency sources are not modified.

## 1.2 adjective forms

The shared renderer accepts class-specific verb/adjective models with the same applicable controls, original-source reset, change highlighting, and construction explanations. Optional adjective bases extend the in-memory Word metadata without changing storage or request formats. Whole-word known IPADIC lattice entries supply class/reading alternatives; no final-い heuristic determines class. A 256-entry cache bounds adjective alternative lookups; dictionary-form readings retain their separate 256-entry cache. Only word-metadata requests do this work.

Adjective recognition matches complete generated forms and source aliases across at most twelve adjacent tokens and eighty characters. Unsupported auxiliary continuations are declined, as are overlaps with saved reading corrections. Original spellings, including contracted な-adjective negatives, are preserved on Reset; changes produce canonical forms. いい／良い and dictionary-backed 不変化型 ～いい compounds receive the よ stem; ordinary かわいい／可愛い retain their regular stem. See the [1.2 audit](release-1.2-audit.md) for current verification.

Contextual command recovery runs only in the word-metadata path, before dictionary-form readings are derived. A separate dictionary helper validates whole-token imperative alternatives against the existing verb generator; its cache holds at most 256 spelling/reading pairs. Only one supported interpretation at an allowed terminal boundary can replace lemma/class/conjugation metadata. Original token surfaces, readings, pronunciation, offsets, and the furigana path are preserved.

## Historical 1.2.0 release boundary

Release date: **28 October 2026**. The full release retains RC1 mimetic artwork. The 1.2 build excluded `public/art/ko-kun/`, which is reserved for future integration; package verification rejects any `art/ko-kun/` entry. Local animation work remains outside the 1.2 release.

## 1.3 selection and invitation

`src/docs-selection.ts` resolves a single Japanese word from supported painted Google Docs selection rectangles and exposed glyph geometry. Selection changes refresh Highlight lookup even without a native selection event; missing, ambiguous and multi-line geometry is declined. Direct non-HTML documents are skipped before overlays or listeners are created. The popup invitation opens the Kōくん settings disclosure and focuses its existing opt-in switch. Dismissal uses `dismissedUpdate:1.3.0` in local storage, synchronized across open popups and retained across restarts.


## v1.4 playground data

Standalone and embedded playgrounds use the same validated playground-data transport. Only the extension playgrounds.html document and top-level HTTP/HTTPS content-script senders may request public local data. The service worker routes bounded requests through offscreen.html to a lazily created playground-data-worker.js, independently of reading-tokenization queues. Online definitions use a separate explicit operation; local operations never invoke automatic fallback.

The deterministic dictionary search builder indexes the verified JMdict shards into search.json.gz: normalized Japanese prefix terms, English inverted postings, and compact result summaries retaining entry IDs and locator buckets. Detail requests load original structured entries and preserve spelling/reading/sense restrictions. Existing compact definition APIs remain unchanged.

Original grammar modules under data/grammar compile into a searchable index, lazy per-point assets, 18 comparisons with 41 complete sentence variants, and a reconciled coverage ledger. Build validation requires all 848 reference IDs, three distinct annotated examples per canonical point, complete notes, and valid links. One explanatory-form alias merges into 847 canonical points. Tokenizer readings are supplemented by contextual authored overrides, including compound numerals. Comparison modules declare their canonical links; lessons retain all linked families and a deduplicated set of related points. Build validation rejects duplicate asset IDs, broken canonical links, incomplete variants, invalid highlights/readings, and malformed activity answers. Metadata includes a separate comparison-content digest. The build never fetches remote grammar content.

Each tool stays mounted during a playground session. Linked vocabulary/form exploration uses temporary views and a return stack. Disposal invalidates pending UI work; search composition and stale results are guarded. Grammar examples carry construction spans and vocabulary targets, so browsing them does not require whole-sentence runtime analysis.
